completed_stage_receipts.summary: Classified maintenance-entry-with-skippable-SOP as a systemic execution-control defect.
Separated ingress reliability from post-entry execution reliability.
Mapped ingress, controller, state, mutation authorization, closure, persistence, resume and cleanup surfaces.
Bound the defect to the recurring policy-present-but-execution-enforcement-incomplete family.
Reused prior learning; the missing mechanism is execution enforcement, not more reminder prose.
Reused the existing controller and deleted the duplicate maintenance_sop implementation.
Rejected recall-only and supervisor-agent fixes; attacked investigate, skip, reopen, checkpoint and closure paths.
Identified durable controller state and closure binding as internal work with no user decision required.
Kept the account hook to cheap triage; detailed SOP remains repository-owned.
Used one controller, one task-local state and existing harness; no new agent, root policy or registry.
Deleted the duplicate SOP and retained only the canonical controller.

reopen_history.reason: Second-order review found that CI validated controller logic but did not directly validate the current durable MAINTENANCE_CONTROLLER_STATE.json, leaving a persisted-state conformance gap.
